newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Second autopsy performed on Bre-X geologist.
newsitem.headline: Second autopsy performed on Bre-X geologist.

text.p: Philippine authorities on Thursday carried out a second autopsy on Michael de Guzman, the Filipino geologist for a Canadian firm that discovered the controversial Busang gold property in Indonesia's jungles.

An initial autoposy on de Guzman, geologist for Bre-X Minerals Ltd, was performed in Indonesia shortly after he fell to his death from a helicopter on his way to the Busang property two weeks ago in North Borneo.
He is to be buried in a Manila cemetery on Friday.
Some Indonesian officials have said de Guzman committed suicide but his brother, Simplicio, said in Manila on Tuesday he saw no reason why his brother would kill himself.
Director Santiago Toledo of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) said his agents carried out the autopsy early on Thursday at the request of de Guzman's parents.
When asked what reason the parents gave for requesting a second autopsy, Toledo told Reuters: "Nothing, it's a regular process."
Toledo said he would know results of the tests next week.
Another brother of de Guzman, Lawrence, confirmed the NBI performed an autopsy on his brother's remains but declined further comment.

The Philippine Embassy in Jakarta said on Wednesday it was waiting to receive from the Indonesian national police a copy of results from the initial autopsy. Bre-X had said the Busang property contained about 71 million ounces of gold, worth $25 billion at current prices, which would make it the century's biggest gold find.
Soon after de Guzman's death, the Toronto-listed firm rocked the international mining community by saying the resources at Busang might be less than previously estimated.
Indonesia's Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana said on Wednesday there was gold at the Busang property but the actual amount had yet to be determined.
